sources.citation: Andrason, Alexander & Pius W. Akumbu. 2024. Conative animal calls in Babanki and Bum (Grassfields languages of Cameroon). Kervan – International Journal of Afro-Asiatic Studies 28(1): 3–28.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent anywhere in the 27-page PDF (a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence: zero hits). Treats Bum as a tone language (Table 1 IPA forms carry H/L tone marks; p. 21 speaks of 'tonal patterns'). Its literature paragraph (p. 4) is the useful thing: 'Bum, in contrast, still lacks systematic studies. The only works that we are aware of comprise of brief discussions of the nominal system (Hyman 1980; Akumbu 2009), a preliminary study of the verb phrase (Bangsi 2016; see also Noumbi 1981), and a dictionary of some 1,800 entries (Ndokobaï, Hedinger, and Akumbu 2023).'

sources.citation: Ndokobaï, Robert Hedinger & Pius W. Akumbu. 2023/2026. Bum Living Dictionary. Living Tongues Institute. https://livingdictionaries.app/bum
sources.note: Landing page read: ~1,800 tone-marked entries (e.g. àduŋ [àdúŋ] 'lizard'); the 'Grammar' tab only says 'please see the Glottolog page for Bum'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0, inventory 1575 'Bum (GM)' (contributor Green & Moran), source: Hedinger, Robert. 2005. Proposed Bum orthography statement. CABTAL Cameroon (unpublished).
sources.note: Segment inventory only (37 C, 7 V, 3 tones); no stress feature. Confirms the 2005 orthography statement is the phonological the deciding source and that it is unpublished.

sources.note: Akumbu's full publication list shows no Bum phonology paper; Bum items are the 2009 noun-class chapter, the 2024 animal-calls paper, the Living Dictionary, and an ELDP Major Documentation Project 'Documentation of Bum' (Feb 2025–Mar 2027) whose ELAR deposit (~56 items, recordings/FLEx) is in progress.
